## Simple explanation

Data preprocessing prepares raw data for a model or analysis. It can
include fixing formats, handling missing values, encoding categories, and
scaling numeric values.

## Technical explanation

Preprocessing transforms features into representations expected by a
learning algorithm. Common operations include parsing, filtering,
normalization, tokenization, imputation, and feature construction. Fitted
transformations should be learned on training data and then applied
consistently to validation, test, and production data.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Preprocessing errors can create data leakage, inconsistent training and
serving behaviour, or inputs that models cannot use. Reproducible
preprocessing is therefore part of the model system, not a one-off
preparation step.

## How it works

Inspect the data and target task, select appropriate transformations, fit
any data-dependent parameters using training data, and apply the resulting
pipeline to other splits and incoming examples. Validate the transformed
outputs and retain the transformation configuration.

## Practical example

A tabular model may impute missing numeric values and standardize features.
The imputation values and scaling parameters are calculated from the
training split, then reused for validation and production records.

## Common misconceptions

- Preprocessing is not always beneficial; unnecessary transformations can
  discard useful information.
- Preprocessing parameters must not be fit using held-out evaluation data.
- The same transformations must be applied at training and inference time.
